title: Time, Coordination, and Consensus
focus: Calculate physical-clock drift, skew, and uncertainty and diagnose conclusions that exceed the available clock contract.

pacing.review: Skim lessons, answer self-checks, and take one generated quiz.
pacing.standard: Study lessons, complete guided practice, use the answer key, and take one or more generated quizzes.
pacing.deep: Complete standard work plus the reinforcement lab and optional project.

lessons.title: Physical Clocks, Drift, Skew, and Uncertainty
Logical Clocks, Vector Clocks, and Causal Order
Safety, Liveness, Failure Detectors, and Consensus Boundaries
Raft Leader Election and Persistent Hard State
Raft Log Replication, Commitment, and Application
Clients, Linearizable Reads, Snapshots, and Compaction
Membership, Leases, Fencing, and Coordination Decisions

learning_outcomes.statement: Calculate physical-clock drift, skew, and uncertainty and diagnose conclusions that exceed the available clock contract.
Derive happened-before, Lamport-clock, and vector-clock relationships without treating display order as causality.
Separate safety, liveness, and failure-detector assumptions and select consensus only for properties that require agreement.
Implement and diagnose Raft elections, persistent hard state, log matching, commitment, and state-machine application.
Implement client deduplication and linearizable reads with explicit ambiguous-outcome and quorum barriers.
Protect snapshots, membership changes, leases, and external resources with atomic state, overlapping quorums, and fencing.
Diagnose eight coordination failures from immutable same-input evidence and scoped safety oracles.
Defend a coordination architecture covering alternatives, operating limits, security, cost, migration, ownership, dissent, and reversal evidence.

lab.note: Use the lab to reinforce the local mechanism; treat expanded matrices and platform-specific evidence as optional deep-dive work.

optional_project.description: Apply Time, Coordination, and Consensus to a small system you know. Write a short design note, experiment report, or implementation summary only if you want deeper practice.
